x: A track match was held between those living North of the Thames and those residing south of the river. Duffett managed the "South" team and Harley the "North" team, and an interesting match was won by the "North" by 4 events to 3.
The Southern Cross Country Championship of 1930, held at Brighton Racecourse, saw Belgrave placed for the first time ever in this event. Warboys (13), Footer (21), Allum (31), Duffett (37), J.
Webb was second to Trodd, T.C.C., in 440 yds., whilst Ernie Duffett gained us a valuable point by finishing 4th, although he pulled a muscle in the first 100 yds.

Then came the Bels- Pyer, Penny, Duffett, Bill Webb and so on, and we won with 77pts, to the 275 of Ashcombe and 276 of TVH. A fortnight later the event moved to Wimbledon where there were over 100 starters, 60 of them Belgravians.
Our scorers were Penny (3rd), Duffett(4th), Mitchell (5th), Cook (7th), Footer (9th) and Rice (15th). South London Harriers (120) were second and Mitcham A.C.
Duffett now ran for us, and … our man picked up three opponents but had to sacrifice two positions and so handed over ninth … Birchfield H had now taken the lead and … were not to be headed again.
